newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to maintain prudent monetary policies.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to maintain prudent monetary policies.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Wednesday the government would maintain prudent monetary policies despite declining inflation.

"The monetary authority will continue to implement prudent monetary policies. Monetary growth needs to be monitored so that it does not put pressure on prices and the balance of payments," he told a parliamentary hearing.
Indonesia has said month-on-month inflation in June fell 0.17 percent, compared with a rise of 0.19 percent in May.
Year-on-year inflation in June was 4.98 percent, compared with 5.08 percent in May.
Indonesia posted an inflation rate of 6.47 percent for the 1996 calendar year against 8.64 percent in 1995. It has forecast inflation at below six percent in 1997.
"Further effort is absolutely needed to bring the inflation down," Djiwandono said, adding that inflation had to be kept low so that nominal interest rates could decline.
He said lower interest rates should help reduce heavy capital inflows due to narrowing interest rate differentials.
"This will help ease an appreciation of the rupiah and improve Indonesian exports in the international market."
